text: me and him dont went to the store yesterday because we was hungry.
note: The original stress-test sentence for the LLM pass — pronoun case (me and him -> he and I), subject-verb agreement (we was -> we were), tense (dont went -> didn't go), plus a dictionary-level contraction fix (dont -> don't).

text: she said i will be there but never showed up
note: Tests whether the model adds punctuation that was 'obviously' missing rather than just fixing words: a missing pair of quotation marks around reported speech, plus a comma before the contrasting clause.

text: i went to the store its a nice day out there dog was happy
note: No punctuation at all, three independent clauses run together, plus a there/their mix-up. Good test of whether the model over-corrects into a single comma-spliced sentence vs. properly splitting it.

text: im not sure what i should work on building next. i think that i def need to work on building the algos out more and make them more advanced.
note: The user's own real dogfooding input, verbatim. Exercises im -> I'm, def -> definitely, and sentence-start capitalization across two sentences in one pass.

text: the dog wagged its tail happily.
note: Guards against a real bug we shipped and caught once already: blindly forcing its -> it's broke correct possessive usage. This sentence is already grammatically correct and MUST come back unchanged (or only re-punctuated), never rewritten.

text: the pizza was great, but i think that i would rather eat steek, though maybe one day i will learn how to cook it on my own.
note: The user's real dogfooding input, verbatim (with their actual 'steek' typo for 'steak'). Originally sat uncorrected until the final period even though it came right after a comma, several words earlier — this is what motivated sending clauses to the LLM at comma boundaries too, not just sentence-ending punctuation. When run through tests/run_tests.py (server-only, no lag window), this exercises the LLM's single-clause-fragment handling rather than the timing fix itself — the timing improvement is only observable in the live browser, not this isolated endpoint test.
